subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
outcomes: I can say Hello!, Hi! and Goodbye!
I can name Fatma, Sami, Lily, Jack, Meg and Tom.
I can hold my pencil well and trace from left to right.

tf.why: Yes! Tom is a cat too.

tf.s: We say Hello! when we meet a friend.
tf.why: Great! Hello! is for meeting people.

tf.s: We say Goodbye! when we meet a friend.
tf.why: We say Goodbye! when we go.

tf.s: We trace from left to right.
tf.why: Yes! Start on the left and go right.

tf.s: We hold a pencil with the whole hand.
tf.why: We use the thumb and two fingers.
Jack is a boy. Meg and Tom are the cats.
Lily is a girl. Meg and Tom are the cats.

boxes.q: Your friend says Hello! You say …
boxes.why: Hi! is a nice answer to Hello!
We say I'm and our name.
In English we go left to right.

boxes.q: At the end of the lesson we say …

boxes.why: Sitting up straight helps us write well.
Hi! is a greeting, like Hello!

hunt.q: Catch a word we say when we meet.
Catch a word we say when we go.
Catch the answer: What's your name?

mcq.why: Meg and Tom are the two cats.
Hello! is how we greet people.

mcq.q: How many fingers hold the pencil with the thumb?
mcq.why: The thumb and two fingers hold the pencil.

mcq.q: Your teacher says: Hello! What's your name? You say …
mcq.why: Say hello back and then your name.

mcq.q: You show your friend a picture of Fatma. You say …
mcq.why: We use This is … to show someone.

mcq.q: The lesson ends. You wave to Meg and say …
mcq.why: We say Goodbye when we go.

mcq.q: Which one is NOT a child?
mcq.why: Tom is a cat, the others are children.

mcq.q: Why do we start tracing at the dot on the left?
o: We write from left to right.
We write from right to left.
mcq.why: English goes from left to right.

mcq.q: Which word does not belong: Hello, Hi, Goodbye, Meg?
mcq.why: Meg is a name; the others are greetings.
